key_idea: Turn the overlap estimate into a density-increment iteration on bipartite 'GCD graphs', using a carefully weighted quality function that rises whenever vertices are restricted to fixed prime-power divisibility classes, until the graph is so structured that the anatomy-of-integers bounds kill the bad pairs.
reason: The reduction to a second-moment bound and the GCD-graph compression argument with its quality increment are a deep, reusable, and surprising idea, and they make clear why many gcd-heavy pairs force shared structure. That core is buried under a long chain of iterative propositions, a case split on R^flat/R^sharp and small/large primes, and many explicit constants (10^2000, exponents 9, 10, 31/30), so the proof is powerful but intricate rather than book-like.
recognized: Koukoulopoulos–Maynard, proof of the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture (Annals 2020)
